chapter: The band, its players and singers
title: Hiring drummer Butch Miles
summary: Basie says he heard Butch Miles with Mel Torme, called him in to fill in after the previous drummer was hurt, and is happy with him as a big band drummer.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: How about the drummer, Butch Miles?
What do you mean, what about him? Why did I hire him?

I don't know, I heard him with Mel and that guy was terrific as a soloist you know, and I still think he is and the more we get along together, the longer we play I mean the tighter everything gets together, (inaudible) as far as being like a big band drummer you know, and I'm very happy with Butch.
Would you say he's got a lot of show biz in him?
Yes, he is. He's a showman and he (inaudible) executes on a solo, but other than that he's still a good band drummer and he's fast becoming a solid big band drummer, you know, which he
had been working with (inaudible) because I don't think he has been exposed to or working too much with big jazz bands. To Have to just lay there and die, and just gut it all night,
Well, you heard Butch then with Mel and then he was leaving Mel or something.
You heard him with somebody else.

No. I didn't get him directly from Mel. They weren't together, and when something happened to the drummer I had, I -- oh, Butch had mentioned -- I saw him someplace, I don't know where it was and he mentioned -- I sort of got hung up, you know.

And he only came over to fill in for this kid that got hurt in Chicago and when he got over here, I mean -- he's here three or four weeks and as far as I'm concerned, he's the guy I was looking for. Although the youngster that I did have, he's a marvelous little drummer and he still is, he still is. He's fine.
Because I hear him all the time, he's with Sammy Davis, Jr..
The one who was in Chicago.
